### Checked records across callback boundaries

Synchronous copied-value callbacks use the same generated dataclasses without
proof fields. If a host callback returns a checked record, wrap it with
`with_recovery(function, value)`, where `value` is a valid record of the exact
declared result type. The package validates the recovery before entering Lean
or invoking the function. Lean then runs the selected record constructor on the
actual reply. Rejection raises `LeanBridgeError`; the recovery is never returned
as successful output.

Checked records produced by Lean arrive at a Python callback as ordinary
proof-free dataclasses. Returned `LeanClosure` values run the selected record
constructor on Python-supplied arguments before their body. This also works in
the tested option, result and array containers, and for a record whose field has
its own selected `Subtype` constructor. A rejected closure call leaves the
closure open for reuse. Retained and asynchronous callbacks and owned checked
records remain unsupported.

The recurring [callback checked-record workflow](https://github.com/seanmorris/lean-bridge/actions/workflows/callback-checked-record-languages.yml)
builds ordinary-source and independently reviewed wheels, removes the author
tree, installs without a registry and runs the independent 26-check consumer.

### Checked records across callback boundaries

Synchronous copied-value callbacks use the same generated structs without proof
fields. If a host closure returns a checked record, pass it through
`with_recovery(callback, value)`, where `value` is a valid record of the exact
declared result type. The crate validates the recovery before entering Lean or
invoking the closure. Lean then runs the selected record constructor on the
actual `Result` reply. Rejection returns `Error::Native`; the recovery is never
returned as successful output.

Checked records produced by Lean arrive at the Rust closure as owned proof-free
structs. Returned `LeanClosure` values run the selected record constructor on
borrowed Rust arguments before their body. This also works in the tested option,
result and vector containers, and for a record whose field has its own selected
`Subtype` constructor. A rejected closure call leaves the closure open for
reuse. Retained and asynchronous callbacks and owned checked records remain
unsupported.

The recurring [callback checked-record workflow](https://github.com/seanmorris/lean-bridge/actions/workflows/callback-checked-record-languages.yml)
builds ordinary-source and independently reviewed crates, removes the author
tree, resolves the prepared dependencies offline and runs the independent
28-check consumer.

Run Python, Ruby and Rust together on Linux x64/glibc 2.38 with Python 3.12,
MRI Ruby 3.3.12 and the pinned Rust 1.90.0 toolchain:

```sh
source scripts/env.sh
LEAN_BRIDGE_CALLBACK_CHECKED_RECORD_LANGUAGE_PROFILES=python,ruby,rust \
  node --test --test-concurrency=1 tests/callback-checked-record-language-installed.test.mjs
```

The test builds ordinary-source and independently reviewed wheels, gems and
crates in two combined releases. It verifies each package-set receipt, removes
the author root, installs from copied archives without registry access and runs
independent consumers. Python and Ruby complete 26 checks per route; Rust
completes 28. They cover proof-free callback arguments, exact typed recovery,
recovery validation before callback entry, record and nested `Subtype` field
constructor rejection, nested option/result replies, returned-closure argument
checks, error preservation, reuse and idempotent close. The default record is
`build/callback-checked-records/languages.json`.
